The environmental problem

Ordinary paper starts as a tree and ends as landfill — and most of it only gets used once along the way.

01

Deforestation

Virgin paper production is one of the leading drivers of forest loss worldwide, cutting down trees that take decades to regrow.

02

Water & energy waste

Turning wood into new paper pulp uses huge amounts of water and electricity — resources that recycled paper skips almost entirely.

03

Landfill overflow

Schools and offices throw away large amounts of usable paper every year instead of giving it a second life.

Mission

Give every sheet a second life

We turn scrap paper that would otherwise be thrown away into notebooks, sheets, and gifts — made by hand, close to home.

Vision

Recycled paper as the standard

A future where reaching for recycled paper isn't the alternative choice — it's simply how paper is made, in every classroom and every desk.

How our product is made

Every sheet goes through the same simple process before it becomes something new.

01

Collect

Scrap paper is gathered from classrooms and offices instead of the trash.

02

Pulp

Paper is shredded and soaked into a soft pulp, no new wood added.

03

Press

Pulp is pressed flat by hand and dried into new sheets.

04

Finish

Sheets are cut, tied, and hand-labeled before they ship out as DaPaper.

the raw sheets

Recycling tips

A few habits that make a real difference.

01

Keep a separate bin at home or school just for scrap paper.

02

Remove staples, clips, and plastic before recycling a sheet.

03

Use both sides of a page before it goes in the bin.

04

Bring your scrap paper to our drop-off point for store credit.

FAQs

Is DaPaper really 100% recycled?

Yes — every sheet is made from collected scrap paper, with no new wood pulp added.

Where does the paper come from?

We collect used paper from classrooms and offices, then pulp and press it into new sheets by hand.

Do you ship outside Guatemala?

Right now we deliver locally — message us on Instagram or TikTok to ask about your area.
